result.topic_en: Differential equations of a geodesic line on the ellipsoid of revolution (latitude, longitude, azimuth) and their reduction to an auxiliary sphere via substitutions A and B, with a spherical-triangle sketch.
result.transcription:
Allgemein ist
$d\varphi = ds.\frac{\cos\zeta(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{a(1-ee)}$
$d\lambda = ds.\frac{\sin\zeta(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{a\cos\varphi}$
$d\zeta = ds.\frac{\sin\zeta(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,tg\,\varphi}{a}$
[Figure: triangle with vertex $\Delta P$, sides $90-\varphi$, $90-\varphi'$, vertices $R$, $R'$, $\Delta Q$]
$\cos R = \cos\zeta\sqrt{\frac{1-ee\sin\varphi^2}{1+\frac{ee}{1-ee}.\cos\varphi^2\sin\zeta^2)(1-ee)}} = \cos\zeta\frac{\sqrt{(1-ee\sin i^2)}}{\sqrt{1-ee}}$
$\sin R = \sin\zeta$ [-$\sqrt{(1+\frac{ee\sin i^2}{tg\zeta^2})}$-] $= \sin\zeta.\sqrt{\frac{1-ee\sin i^2}{1-ee\sin\varphi^2}}$
$tg\,R = \frac{\tan\zeta\sqrt{(1-ee)}}{\sqrt{(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)}}$
Man setze [-$\sqrt{\frac{1-ee}{1-ee\sin\varphi}} = A$-]
[-$A\,tg\zeta = tg\,R$-]
[-$\frac{\cos\zeta.\sqrt{(1-ee)}}{a\cos R} = B = const.$-]
[-$d\varphi = \frac{B\,ds}{A\ldots}$ $\frac{d\lambda}{d\zeta} = \ldots$-]
$\sqrt{\frac{1-ee\sin\varphi^2}{1-ee}} = A$; $\frac{a\cos R}{\cos\zeta\sqrt{(1-ee)}} = B = Const. = \frac{a}{\sqrt{(1-ee)}.\sqrt{(1-ee\cos i^2)}}$ [?]
$\frac{tg\zeta}{A} = tg\,R$ $\quad dQ = \frac{A^3}{B}.ds$
$\partial\lambda = \frac{\partial P}{A}$
$\partial\zeta = \frac{\partial R}{A}$

methods.what: Differential equations of a geodesic on an ellipsoid of revolution (latitude, longitude, azimuth)
Transformation of azimuth to auxiliary-sphere angle R
Expressions for cos R and sin R in terms of the constant i (Clairaut-type constant)
Substitution A and constant B relating ellipsoid geodesic to sphere; arc element, longitude and azimuth differentials
Relations between differentials of longitude/azimuth and spherical quantities
